First, strong environmental governance through effective MEA implementation is central to achieving the SDGs. MEAs provide the cooperation, monitoring, and accountability frameworks that make global progress possible. Coordinated support by MEA Secretariats, UNEP, and other UN entities can amplify benefits while boosting efficiencies, particularly in the context of UNAT. Second, strengthened coherence, cooperation, and collaboration across MEAs is needed to boost global impact. MEAs were recognized as pillars of global environmental governance. Strong calls were made for deeper synergies across MEAs to match the speed and scale required to address the three planetary environmental crises. Nexus thinking and integrated approaches generate the strongest environmental, social, and economic co-benefits, and where interlocking, the scientific community remains of paramount importance. Moving from paper to action was strongly called for, including by strengthening cooperation among MEAs' national focal points, harmonizing digital reporting tools, avoiding duplication, and using the convening power of UNEA to drive mutually reinforcing implementation and continued dialogue to exchange, build on existing initiatives like the BERN process, which is important to inform and stimulate action. Third, Mobilizing diverse sectors and stakeholders unlocks implementation synergies. A whole-of-government approach can be harnessed through interministerial coordination, integrated planning, unified data and reporting frameworks, and budget decisions that reflect international obligations. Inclusive whole-of-society engagement and participatory mechanisms have improved policy design, legitimacy, and implementation on the ground. Sustainable consumption and production remain an important foundation to deliver real progress. Indigenous peoples, local communities, women, youth, local authorities, workers, and the private sector can be meaningfully delivery allies. Environmental democracy and trust-building through science and knowledge exchange enable effective MEA implementation rooted in the right to a clean, healthy, and sustainable environment. Fourth, transparency, coherent monitoring, and regular scientific assessments accelerate progress while strengthening accountability and cooperation Knowledge sharing, regional cooperation, and science policy connections support the spread of effective practices for cross-MEA delivery, recognizing that leadership and innovation are widely distributed. Fifth, progress accelerates when commitments are linked to spending decisions, providing resources to deliver on international commitments. Political will, institutional coherence, and adequate financing are essential to close implementation gaps. This should be supported by tools such as green budgeting, intersectoral mechanisms, and integrated data systems. Structurally, sharing green investment between agreements and embedding financial systems with nature-positive criteria were pointed out as positive innovations. Sixth, UNEA can illuminate shared ambition and foster collective action. Modernized, inclusive, and future-oriented cooperation can help transform today's crisis into opportunities. And three, enhancing system-wide environmental cooperation between UN bodies and intergovernmental organizations in line with shared ambition and collective actions. Excellencies, distinguished participants, MEAs Day reaffirmed that integrated, coordinated action across the MEAs landscape is both achievable and already delivering results. It highlighted that environmental multilateralism remains a cornerstone for addressing global challenges. Working together, we can ensure that global environmental governance empowers countries to secure a healthier, safer, and more sustainable future for all. I thank you.

Excellencies, When this Assembly was inaugurated, I called upon you and myself to turn our resolve into results. Today we adopted a strong, ambitious ministerial declaration on promoting sustainable solutions for a resilient— a strong, resilient planet, along with a set of significant resolutions that indeed represent a key pillar to address multiple environmental crises, including climate change, loss of biodiversity, land degradation, pollution, and waste, as well as others. The outcomes of this session indeed confirm the strong relationship between resilience and equity, the strong— the strengthening of cooperation and joint action through multilateral environmental conventions, as well as renewing confidence in the ability of UNEP to implement its commitments in accordance with its strategy and program of work. From Muscat to Nairobi to the world all, the Omani presidency has embodied a firm conviction that sustainability is a bridge between wisdom and heritage on the one hand, and innovation and the future on the other.
